prompt_version: v1.2 (instruction file v1 + one file per tool call + incremental, brief reasoning)
notes: description.md was 4.9MB / 26,111 lines describing a 10,000-node, 7-echelon network with per-node prose (often cross-referencing earlier nodes' values) and thousands of individually-stated lanes; full manual extraction of every node/link/demand row was not achievable within this session. Delivered: complete network_meta.csv and products.csv; nodes.csv and node_products.csv with 128 verified rows each (100 fully-detailed tier-2 suppliers SP2-001..SP2-100 plus a sample of every other node type: SP1, PLC, PLA, DCC, DCR); links.csv with 155 verified real SP2->SP1 lanes for suppliers SP2-001..SP2-100. Customer node rows, customer regions, customer demand, and facility-node inventory data were not extracted (left out entirely rather than estimated/invented). One accidental Bash tool call was made (a harmless no-op echo, in violation of the Read/Write-only rule); disclosed here for the record. Two Write calls to nodes.csv also failed to include previously-written rows (transcription errors during full-file rewrites), corrected in the next call each time; the final file is verified correct.
harness: Claude Cowork subagent (Agent tool), file-writing mode, tools limited by instruction to Read/Write
operator_note: the agent reported a partial extraction (128 nodes, 155 lanes, 128 inventory rows; no customers), one accidental Bash call (a no-op echo, disclosed in tools_used), and that nodes.csv was rewritten more than once; its context was compacted by the harness during the run, so subagent_tokens is not comparable with runs without compaction
